rationale: This is a one-leg cosmetic substitution (capx → ΔPPEGT) on the already-tested "Termed-Out Investment Financing," keeping the same net-LT-issuance and falling-short-debt legs and the same mechanism, so it is a near-rediscovery rather than a substantive refinement.

Identical in structure and mechanism to the archived "Deleveraging Productive Expansion" with only the investment proxy swapped from ΔPPENT+ΔINVT to ΔPPEGT, and the parent already showed economically negligible alpha (0.004, t=0.47), so the variant is both derivative and unpromising.

The economics (unused secured debt capacity) are coherent, but the construction merely stacks the legs of two already-tested signals into a four-way MIN of ranks, which mechanically collapses to the weakest leg, concentrates the long portfolio in a thin, tangible-heavy/low-leverage subset, and risks apparent gains from unstable composition rather than a new mechanism.

Direct re-proposal of the archived "Maturity-Downgrade Investment" with capx replaced by ΔPPEGT while the two financing legs are unchanged, so it adds no new economic content beyond a proxy substitution.

Beyond being a bolt-together of two archive signals, the third leg is mechanically collinear with the second (same numerator) and its high values mostly identify firms with negative retained earnings, so the signal largely re-expresses the known loss-firm/low-profitability anomaly rather than a novel financing-investment interaction.

Substituting the within-firm inventory level state for the inventory flow in the archived "Externally Funded Inventory-Workforce Divergence" is economically defensible (unsold stock during retrenchment vs. growth investment), but it remains a single-leg variant of an already-evaluated signal and inherits its weak cross-sectional evidence (fmb t = 0.51), so it does not constitute a substantively different improvement.
